questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car, what happens?

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they use their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You stop other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they use their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when following a car. This way, the driver will see you in their rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirror much more often than their side mirror.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, what should you do?

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle works fine.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: A small problem on a motorcycle is more serious than on a car. Always check your motorcycle thoroughly before you ride.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, why should you ride in the left portion of your lane?

options.text: It helps you see better ahead.
It makes it harder to see ahead.
It blocks your view of the vehicle.
It lets the other driver go faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you a better view ahead and makes you more visible to drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while riding?

options.text: Keep riding and hope to wake up.

questions.explanation: Do not ride when you are tired. On long trips, take a rest break at least every two hours to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.
Make sure other drivers cannot see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Good lane position should help you see others and be seen by them. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your chance of a crash?

options.text: Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.
Signal only when you want to.
Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To prevent crashes, make sure others can see you. Signal your turns clearly. Use your brake light. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always watch the road ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Be loose and flap in the wind.
Only partially cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Good protective clothing must cover your arms and legs completely. Wear clothes that fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in a crash.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's brake light compare to a car's brake light?
questions.explanation: A motorcycle brake light is not as noticeable as a car's brake light. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop to help other drivers notice you are braking.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other regulation signs are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if clothes are very loose and flap in the wind.
Yes, if your jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if your jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: The right clothing reduces injury in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, are made of strong material, and fit snugly without flapping in the wind.

questions.question: In a no passing zone, what can a motorcycle do?

options.text: A motorcycle can still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle can pass if it finishes before another vehicle comes.
A motorcycle can pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: No passing zones mean no vehicle can pass. You also cannot pass by driving off the main road.

questions.question: What is the main active ingredient in marijuana?
questions.explanation: The main active substance in marijuana is THC (tetrahydrocannabinol).

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle before every ride to stay safe.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect you from?
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face from injury in a crash and from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and rocks thrown from other vehicles.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders turn their heads to look over their shoulders before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
They can get other drivers' attention by turning their heads.
They should make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot see. Always turn your head to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When should a pre-ride inspection be done?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This takes a few minutes and prevents dangerous problems. Small issues on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When should a pre-ride inspection be done?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. It takes just a few minutes and helps prevent dangerous situations.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping a group of riders small?

options.text: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
A small group can break traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always try to catch up to the group.
It will be hard to know where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
questions.explanation: Small groups have advantages. Other vehicles can pass a small group safely. A small group is less likely to get separated by traffic or traffic lights. Slower riders do not need to rush to catch up.

questions.question: Before every ride, check all of these except:
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle carefully. Check the rims and spokes for bends, looseness, or damage. Check tire condition and tread. Check all lights.

questions.question: Why are signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They don't matter much because motorcycles are small.
They tell other drivers what you plan to do.
You only need to use them if other vehicles are nearby.
They work differently than signals on cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are at risk. Use your turn signals to tell other drivers your plans. Always signal when you change lanes or turn, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required equipment on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Nevada law requires motorcycles to have one or two headlights, a red taillight, a brake light, at least one rear reflector, front and rear brakes, turn signals (if made after 1973), mirrors on each handlebar, fenders on both wheels, footrests, a horn, and a muffler.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. How can you be more visible?

options.text: Weave back and forth while riding.

questions.explanation: Most crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day, to help others see you.

questions.question: Which clothing item will NOT help protect you in a crash?
questions.explanation: To reduce injury, wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Use durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Skip the jacket if the weather is warm.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
Wear shorts when it's hot outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket made of good material when riding, even in warm weather. A jacket helps protect you and prevents dehydration. Also wear long pants and tuck in your shoelaces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.
